# Configuration

`.triad-plus/team.json` separates stable role IDs from user-facing names and
personas. A schema-version-1 configuration has four role records:

```json
{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "interaction": { "language": "English", "owner_name": "Owner", "communication_style": "concise" },
  "roles": {
    "orchestrator": { "displayName": "Coordinator", "persona": "calm and precise", "model": null, "reasoning_effort": null },
    "developer": { "displayName": "Builder", "persona": "methodical", "model": null, "reasoning_effort": null },
    "reviewer": { "displayName": "Critic", "persona": "independent", "model": null, "reasoning_effort": null },
    "evaluator": { "displayName": "Evaluator", "persona": "fresh and evidence-led", "model": null, "reasoning_effort": null, "enabled": false }
  }
}
```

`orchestrator`, `developer`, and `reviewer` are the Core roles. `evaluator` is
optional and enabled only when `roles.evaluator.enabled` is `true`. Omitting that
field is backward-compatible and means Evaluator+ is not configured.

When enabled, Evaluator+ is automatically dispatched by the Orchestrator after
Triad reaches Reviewer approval. It receives a fresh post-run packet and cannot
change the closed Triad result. Set `enabled` to `false` to disable this default.

For a schema-v1 installation, the runtime adapter is selected once per
installed control workspace (`--host`) and all roles use that adapter. A
schema-v2 installation can record multiple project-local adapters, but this
does not yet select a host per Attempt: no host is inferred from install order,
and dispatch is explicitly unsupported until Attempt-bound liveness and
selection are implemented. The team file records role-level models and effort,
while generated profiles inherit host defaults. A requested model is not an
attestation of host selection or availability. A blank model means no request. Never put
tokens, API keys, or private deployment data in this file.

## Installation ownership and version

The package version and the installed workspace version are separate facts:

```bash
npx triad-plus --version
npx triad-plus version --control /path/to/project-control
```

After successful materialization, `.triad-plus/installation.json` records the
adapter (schema v1) or adapter membership plus per-adapter exact assets and
shared-path owner sets (schema v2), scopes, SHA-256 hashes, timestamps, and a
deterministic fingerprint. Project paths are control-workspace-relative; global
paths identify the user-level managed asset. Read-only commands do not migrate
v1. An explicit successful `adapter add ... --apply` is the v1-to-v2 migration
boundary.

The manifest deliberately does not own `.triad-plus/team.json`, `.loop/`,
`project.yaml`, feature cards, artifacts, evidence, or product source. A failed
install never writes a success manifest. Legacy workspaces are migrated by
`upgrade --apply` using the currently executing package version; the previous
version is not guessed.

When a team configuration is materialized, the managed role-run block in
`AGENTS.md` is recorded as a bounded block asset. Uninstall removes that block
only when its markers and hash still match, never the surrounding user file.
Global assets are shared-capable and therefore preserved by default by
`uninstall --global`.

`doctor` reports CLI version, installed version, manifest state, adapter, and
project/global scope. `adapter list` and `adapter doctor` inspect v1/v2 state
without writes; host executable availability is separate from recorded adapter
membership. `adapter add`, `adapter upgrade`, and `adapter remove` operate on
project-local assets only. Remove and upgrade are dry runs unless `--apply` is
present, modified or conflicting bytes are preserved and block false success,
and no command creates global Triad assets by default. The host-native
`.triad-runtime/adapter.json` singleton remains unchanged when adding another
adapter; additional metadata is stored per adapter and is not a dispatch seam.
Codex/Hermes project-local native entries remain limited or unproven. The CLI
reports these limitations instead of claiming parity. Version skew is explicit
and npm `latest` is never queried.

## Configure models through the agent

The installed `triad-model-configuration` skill lets an owner ask the selected
agent to show or change role models without editing host-specific files. The
agent reads `.triad-runtime/adapter.json`, validates `.triad-plus/team.json`,
changes only the explicitly requested `model` or `reasoning_effort` fields, and
reports the request separately from the effective host configuration. It never
invents model IDs or puts credentials in configuration.

Generated agent assets use **host default** for model and effort on every
adapter. Triad+ cannot verify an arbitrary ID against every host's available
providers before that host loads its files. An unknown native override can
prevent the host from starting the command at all. Therefore setup and upgrade
omit managed `model`, `variant`, `reasoningEffort`, and Codex
`model_reasoning_effort` overrides; canonical requests remain unchanged in
`team.json`, including legacy invalid requests so they can be corrected.

The wizard rejects model IDs with spaces/control characters, and OpenCode
requests must use its `provider/model` form. These are syntax checks only;
passing them does not mean a provider or model is available. Use the host's
native model picker to inspect available IDs and select the session model.
Triad+ must report that selection as unobservable unless the host supplies
reliable evidence. Reasoning/variant names are host-specific and are never
translated between providers.

Existing installations need the normal managed upgrade (with its preview and
explicit apply) to remove old overrides. Do not manually patch generated
agent files or edit an installation manifest to hide drift. Existing user-level Codex TOML profiles are not rewritten by the current
skill/wrapper installation; any remediation of those files requires an explicit
path preview and consent. The model configuration skill records requests; it does not claim that
`upgrade --apply` applies the requested model.

## Guided readiness and explicit consent

Run `npx triad-plus preflight --host <adapter> --control .` for one-at-a-time
correction and confirmation. `--non-interactive --json` returns actionable
failures without granting consent. Native entries use the same checks, with
explicit host capability limits. Confirmed catalogs remain per repository and
are independently checked before dispatch/verifier execution. See
[universal readiness](universal-readiness.md) for receipts, current-state-bound
approvals, model limitations, automation and upgrade constraints.

## Inactive quality-gate proposals

Setup also prepares an inactive `.triad-plus/quality-gates.draft.json` from
mapped manifests. Inspect it with `npx triad-plus quality-gates --control .`;
it never activates commands or replaces `.loop/quality-gates.yaml`. Use
`--lint` for structure-only validation without execution. See
[quality-gate discovery](quality-gate-discovery.md) for sources, per-worktree
binding, exclusions and the remaining guided-confirmation limitations.

## Retry and scope policy

New control workspaces use separate finite budgets for environment recovery and
candidate remediation. Existing workspaces that only declare
`max_rework_attempts_per_item` retain that legacy policy. A card may optionally
bind a versioned JSON scope contract at its first assignment; without one, the
deterministic scope preflight is not configured and independent review remains
the semantic scope check. See [verification.md](verification.md) for the
contract and matching rules.

Cards may also declare `required_gates` as an additive list of trusted
repository gate IDs. Globally required gates are never suppressed; a selected
optional gate becomes required for that card, and an absent or empty list keeps
the legacy gate behavior. Selected IDs are validated before Developer dispatch
and are bound to the assignment; Triad does not attach visual or other
domain-specific meaning to a gate ID.

## Optional immutable Quality Contract

New or upgraded control workspaces may set:

```yaml
project:
  quality_contract:
    baseline: artifacts/quality-baseline.json
    fingerprint: <sha256 of the canonical manifest>
```

The JSON manifest must contain at least one hashed, project-relative source and
may contain criteria scoped only to `product_quality` or `delivery_closure`.
The fingerprint is deterministic and independent of JSON whitespace or object
key order. A configured contract is validated before expensive verification
gates; malformed manifests and source drift fail closed. Omitting the section
preserves the 1.7 legacy PRD baseline behavior. A rebaseline is a new manifest
revision and explicit owner event, never an in-place edit.

# Evaluator+

Evaluator+ is optional and outside the Triad production loop. Configure
`roles.evaluator.enabled: true` and the Orchestrator automatically invokes it
only after the Reviewer has approved a feature or delivery.

It receives the goal, acceptance target, final artifact, and verifier evidence.
It should not receive developer reasoning, prior reviewer conversation, or
attempt history unless the owner explicitly requires it. It reports `PASS`,
`FAIL`, or `INDETERMINATE`, with concise evidence references, under
`artifacts/evaluator-plus/`.

An Evaluator+ `FAIL` does not reopen Triad, change the approved state, or start
repair. An owner or a later Orchestrator may use it as input to a new run.

When a project declares an immutable Quality Contract, the packet also carries
the approved Quality Baseline fingerprint and exactly one result for each
`product_quality` criterion. `delivery_closure` criteria are deliberately
excluded and are evaluated by delivery closure. The control plane validates
fingerprint, candidate binding, criterion coverage, and the deterministic
aggregate (`FAIL` over `INDETERMINATE` over `PASS`) before recording the report.
Formatting a manifest or changing a bound source invalidates the contract; it
never starts a product retry.

# Getting started

Triad+ keeps project-control records in a dedicated **Control Workspace**,
separate from product repositories. The terminal wizard is the normal
first-run path; it does not scan sibling folders or create a PRD, quality
gates, repository commits, or worktrees for you.

For a single procedural OpenCode journey from an empty Control Workspace to
reading the reports and Cockpit, follow the
[OpenCode first-loop tutorial](tutorials/opencode-first-loop.md).

## 1. Install and onboard

Start from a directory outside the product repository, then launch the wizard:

```bash
mkdir triad-control && cd triad-control
npx triad-plus
```

Choose **New workspace** and confirm this separate Control Workspace root.
The product-repository screen lists read-only immediate-child Git roots with
their current branches. Use Up/Down to focus, Space to select, and Enter to
confirm one or more repositories; Enter with none selected explains the
required action. Use **Add repository by path** for an explicitly supplied
existing local Git root outside that list, or choose **Set up a new
repository** / **Skip repository setup for now**. For selected repositories,
the wizard groups the suggested ID, folder, base branch, project branch, and
worktree mapping for review; press Enter to accept those values or type `edit`
to change them through the validated prompts. Greenfield setup asks how many
repositories to create and presents the same grouped defaults. New local Git
repositories are initialized only after the final approval; setup does not
create their initial commits or worktrees. The selected path and detected
base branch are shown in the mapping step. Final approval records repository
mappings and installs adapter assets; recording a worktree path does not
create that worktree or establish project readiness.

Select one or more harnesses on the next checkbox screen with the same keys:
OpenCode, Codex, Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, Antigravity, and Hermes Agent.
The first harness selected is visibly marked as primary because it supplies
the current singleton runtime metadata; multi-harness installation does not
provide per-Attempt cross-harness dispatch. Escape cancels from repository
selection and goes back from harness selection. Ctrl+C exits without applying
the plan. The concise confirmation can be expanded with `details`; when a
user-level entry is selected, reviewing its exact paths is required before
typing exactly `install` to apply the plan. The selected adapter's project assets can be installed
without its native host executable being present; setup does not probe host
availability. An additional optional screen can select the Codex `$triad` or
Hermes `/triad` user-level entry. The concise plan can be expanded with
`details`; when a user-level entry is selected, that exact-path review is
required before `install` is accepted. Skipping it leaves user-level files
unchanged. The wizard does not clone repositories or push changes. For full
setup behavior and limitations, see
[npx installation](npx-installation.md). Selecting an adapter does not prove
native host discovery or route an Attempt to that host. See the
[adapter compatibility matrix](compatibility.md).

The six adapter choices describe installable host assets, not six validated
native sessions. The current release acceptance is one OpenCode 1.19.3
host-default E2E. Requested model/effort values remain intent: generated role
assets omit unverified overrides, and the live OpenCode Orchestrator, Developer,
and Reviewer shared the same session default. Choose/confirm the host default
explicitly in preflight; READY is not model identity or per-role routing proof.

## 2. Add the project inputs and check readiness

At the Control Workspace root, create `PRD.md` with a small goal, one
observable acceptance criterion, and a deterministic verification command.
Make an initial commit in each mapped repository and create the declared
worktree. Run `npx triad-plus preflight --host <adapter> --control .` (or enter
through the native command) to confirm models/defaults, select/edit/reject gates
and confirm prerequisites one action at a time. Existing manual
`.loop/quality-gates.yaml` can be reviewed as a catalog; it is not required when
approved per-repository catalogs are generated by preflight. See
[guided readiness](universal-readiness.md). Setup does not create these
inputs implicitly. It does prepare an inactive per-repository gate draft from
mapped manifests. Inspect it with `npx triad-plus quality-gates --control .`;
no discovered commands are executed or activated. See
[quality-gate discovery](quality-gate-discovery.md) before selecting or editing
a catalog. Immediately after install, the wizard gives these staged
next steps and an optional host/install diagnostic command; it does not imply
that project readiness has been established. Follow this
[quickstart](../README.md#one-quickstart-root-control-workspace-and-root-prd)
for the documented first-run path. The wizard's first-run summary is an
installation plan; it does not inspect or attest to project readiness, probe
host availability, assess PRD or gate quality, or execute gates. Check the
project inputs separately. `doctor` diagnoses selected adapter installation,
managed assets, the host executable, and available host/verifier configuration;
it is not a readiness check and does not run quality gates.

Run `doctor` separately for host and installation diagnostics:

```bash
npx triad-plus doctor --host opencode --control .
```

Resolve structural gaps from the preview yourself, and address any host or
installation issue reported by `doctor`. Open OpenCode in the Control
Workspace and start the loop with `/triad ./PRD.md` (or `/triad` to use the
root PRD). Bootstrap snapshots the source to immutable
`artifacts/prd.md` and records its SHA-256; keep the source unchanged. Direct
`init` remains available for scripts and advanced setup, but is not the
first-run wizard path. A successful `init --host ... --control ...`
confirms installation of adapter assets, **not** creation of `project.yaml`,
root `PRD.md`, quality gates, or mapped Git worktrees. Do not infer loop
readiness from adapter installation alone. The declared deterministic gates
are run later by `triad-verify` for an Attempt's recorded candidate.

## 3. Follow the Card and evidence

The normal path is:

```text
Orchestrator → Developer → verifier evidence → Reviewer → approved | rework | blocked
```

The Reviewer considers the Card, diff, Developer report, and verifier evidence.
A declared `in_progress` state is not proof that an agent is currently active;
Triad+ does not record agent liveness. See the [operating guide](operating-guide.md)
and the [Italian operating guide](operating-guide.it.md).

### Optional: plan draft PR delivery

Before the first Developer assignment, the Orchestrator can show an opt-in PR
grouping plan and request **one explicit owner approval** of its structure.
After normal Card verification and independent review, the approved structure
can be reused with fresh, byte-bound evidence to prepare draft PRs; no further
structural approval is needed unless the scope changes. This requires separately
prepared snapshots and exact group branch/worktree bindings, and never
authorizes automatic merge or release. The default manual delivery path is
unchanged. See [PR planning and prerequisites](pr-planning.md).

## 4. Read the Markdown reports

When canonical Card, attempt, verifier, and Reviewer records are available, the
Orchestrator can explicitly invoke the deterministic report renderer to write
`card-reports/<card-id>.md` and `handoff.md`. The renderer being available does
not mean those files have been generated: absent outputs remain absent until
the renderer is invoked with derived context. They are portable, read-only
views, not new approval evidence. See the [human-readable reports guide](human-readable-reports.md)
for the required context and commands.

## 5. Open Cockpit after data exists

After the Control Workspace contains project/Card/attempt data, open the local
read-only Cockpit:

```bash
npx triad-plus cockpit
```

From the Control Workspace, Cockpit validates the current directory and opens
the one-time loopback URL in a local interactive browser when safe. The URL is
always printed; use `--no-open` to disable automatic opening or
`--control <path>` to select a workspace explicitly. Cockpit shows persisted
records and evidence; it does not start agents or provide liveness monitoring.
For its security and data interpretation details, see the [Cockpit guide](../cockpit/README.md).

# Refresh an existing Codex or Hermes global entry

Use a trusted Triad+ package to refresh an already owned global entry after a
project upgrade. This does not install a new entry, select a model, migrate a
profile, run discovered commands or start the engineering loop.

```bash
# Read-only: use the same exact Control Workspace and host profile for both steps.
npx triad-plus entry refresh --host codex --control /absolute/control-workspace

# Inspect every absolute file path and before/after hash in the preview.
# Only after explicit owner consent, copy the current Expected state value:
npx triad-plus entry refresh --host codex --control /absolute/control-workspace \
  --apply --expected-state <sha256-from-this-preview>
```

For Hermes substitute `--host hermes`; select the actual active profile before
preview. `HERMES_HOME` selects where Hermes stores/loads the native skill. The
trusted preflight wrapper and binding use the canonical `$HOME/.hermes` path,
including with named profiles. Changing `HOME`, `CODEX_HOME`, `HERMES_HOME`, the
active Hermes profile, installation ownership or project/global bytes can
invalidate the request.
Do not search profiles or substitute a different workspace after approval.
No terminal prompt is required: without `--apply` this command is read-only;
automation with absent/stale `--expected-state` fails nonzero without writing.
The hash binds the explicit CLI operation, not cryptographic human identity.
Agents must not infer owner consent from a hash or auto-apply a preview.

The current workspace must already match the trusted package's project asset
membership, bytes and version. The command will not bless local code merely
because its hash appears in an edited manifest. A supported legacy single-adapter
project upgrade can be performed separately with `upgrade --host <host> --control
<path> --apply`, after reviewing its own dry run. That upgrade does not silently
refresh the global binding. Older multi-adapter installs requiring coordinated
shared project changes remain a separate limitation; this command does not
waive or bypass their upgrade refusal.

The preview lists the exact existing native skill/wrapper files and the binding
for this workspace, plus the local manifest to update. Only recorded files whose
current bytes still match prior ownership may be replaced. Missing, modified,
unowned, symlinked or foreign-workspace entries stop. A legacy prompt collision
is preserved. If shared wrapper/skill bytes would change and other workspace
bindings or adapter owners exist, stop for a separately reviewed coordinated
operation; this command does not refresh other workspaces implicitly. If those
shared bytes are already current, only this workspace's stale binding may change.

Application rechecks the plan before writes and project/profile/ownership before
committing the manifest. It retains original file permissions, uses atomic file
replacement and backs up old bytes under the selected Control Workspace's
`.triad-plus/backups/entry-refresh-*`. `plan.json` maps backup files to exact target
paths; `installation.json` is the prior manifest. Temporary files beside listed
global targets are removed. On failure, earlier replacements are restored only
when their bytes still match this operation; concurrent edits are preserved and
reported for local recovery. Backups remain available after success or failure.
This is not a crash-atomic transaction across multiple files: if interrupted,
the native guard must block inconsistent state. Inspect the backups and exact
files before an explicitly authorized recovery; do not patch hashes to bypass it.

Unchanged entries are idempotent: no new backups, manifest writes or repeated
readiness confirmations. A successful refresh says only that these entry files
and owner binding were refreshed. Run the usual preflight through the trusted
wrapper afterward. Workspace READY, runtime availability, effective model
identity and per-role routing remain distinct. Tests execute the installed
wrapper/preflight on controlled workspaces; they do not prove a provider session
or the still-required native harness E2E.

# Human-readable reports

Triad+ keeps JSON/YAML control records, verification evidence, review reports,
candidate fingerprints, and delivery records as the source of truth. From those
records the Orchestrator can materialize two portable Markdown views:

- one `card-reports/<card-id>.md` for every terminal Card;
- one final delivery handoff with a human-first summary and links to the Card
  reports.

The report renderer is deterministic and does not make an additional LLM call.
It attributes changed paths to the complete Card baseline, so a rework attempt
does not hide files changed by an earlier attempt. Reports contain relative
evidence references and redact unrelated absolute paths.

An available renderer is not proof that a report file exists: the Orchestrator
must invoke the CLI with derived context. Until then, `card-reports/<card-id>.md`
and `handoff.md` are **not materialized**; if an expected output is absent, do
not describe it as generated. The Cockpit and these reports are views of the
canonical records, not new approval evidence.

## Materialize a Card report

The Orchestrator first writes a small derived JSON context from the canonical
Card, attempt, verifier, Reviewer, and delivery records. The source Card and
those records remain read-only. Then run:

```bash
node .triad-runtime/triad-human-report.mjs \
  --mode card \
  --project /absolute/path/to/control-workspace \
  --input .loop/runtime/report-context/CARD-001.json \
  --output card-reports/CARD-001.md \
  --worktree /absolute/path/to/product-worktree \
  --base-commit <card-baseline-commit>
```

For an approved Card the renderer requires a final commit, the candidate
fingerprint recorded by passing verifier evidence, independent Reviewer
approval, and the complete changed-path manifest. Current verifier evidence
also carries a `candidate_manifest` with the verified paths and content hashes.
The renderer binds that manifest to the final commit delta (allowing the
expected `git_head` change caused by the commit) and records the resulting
committed fingerprint separately. A blocked or not-delivered terminal Card must
include a truthful reason and never claims delivery. Writes are atomic and
re-running the command with the same context is idempotent.

### Card context checklist

The derived card context should carry only canonical control-plane fields:

- `card.id` (and its title, goal/outcome, repository, and card path);
- terminal `status`, `attempts`, and verification runs;
- at least one passing verification run with its evidence path and candidate
  fingerprint;
- independent `review.decision: approved` and its evidence/fingerprint;
- `final.branch`, `final.commit`, `final.repository`, `final.base_commit`, and
  `final.candidate_fingerprint`;
- assignment/packet/verification provenance and bounded evidence references.

For an approved card, `final.candidate_fingerprint` is the pre-commit
fingerprint recorded by the passing verifier. The renderer computes and records
`final.committed_candidate_fingerprint` from the committed delta; do not replace
the verified fingerprint with a newly calculated value in the input context.
The source card and canonical evidence remain read-only.

### Attempt-local Reviewer references

When a Card report input already includes an attempt-local Reviewer file in
that Attempt's `evidence_refs`, the report places a safe relative link in that
Attempt's row. It does not invent a reference, read the Markdown to derive a
verdict, or promote the document to a validated approval. The singular
`review` object remains a **Card-level** Reviewer section and must not be read
as a decision for every Attempt. References are linked only when they resolve
to an existing regular file inside the declared project or worktree root and
the generated URL remains within that root; otherwise the report retains a
plain, redacted path.

## Materialize the final handoff

```bash
node .triad-runtime/triad-human-report.mjs \
  --mode handoff \
  --project /absolute/path/to/control-workspace \
  --input .loop/runtime/report-context/delivery.json \
  --output handoff.md
```

The handoff opens with the executive summary and Card results, then preserves
links to the technical evidence, branch/commit map, quality-contract closure,
Evaluator+ result, delivery gates, demo details, risks, and practical test.
It is a view for people, not an alternative delivery state machine.

When the output exists, its Card-report links are relative to `handoff.md`, and
explicit local evidence references are linked relative to that output. A report
or evidence file that was not supplied, does not exist, is external, or fails
path-safety checks remains unlinked; generating the handoff does not create
the underlying canonical evidence.

### Handoff context checklist

The derived handoff context must include a non-empty `cards` list and a
`decision` plus `executive_summary`. Each card entry carries `id`, `title`,
`status`, `summary`, `report_path`, and, when available, `commit`,
`candidate_fingerprint`, `verification`, `review`, `evaluator_report`, and
`evidence_refs`. The remaining canonical handoff fields are:

`code_areas`, `residual`, `verification`, `review`, `branch_commits`,
`practical_test`, `evaluator`, `delivery`, `quality_contract`,
`delivery_criteria`, `demo`, `evidence_refs`, `exceptions`, `prd_baseline`,
`approved_cards`, `push_evidence`, `gate_metrics`,
`local_worktree_integration`, `delivery_closure_record`, `final_message`,
`risks`, and `generated_from`.

Populate fields from canonical run, card, verifier, Reviewer, Evaluator+, and
delivery records. Do not pass Developer reasoning, queue-control narrative, or
unbounded source documents merely to satisfy the renderer.

# Install Triad+

Triad+ installs a project-control workspace, not application code. Keep it
outside product repositories whenever possible.

For the recommended first-run journey from wizard through PRD, evidence,
Markdown reports, and Cockpit, see [Getting started](getting-started.md).

```bash
npx triad-plus
```

The terminal wizard is the normal setup and management path. If the current
directory contains a valid Control Workspace manifest, it defaults to managing
that workspace. Otherwise it defaults to creating a new workspace; selecting
management then requires an explicit existing path. It never searches sibling
directories.

### New-workspace onboarding

For a new workspace, the wizard asks for a Control Workspace root. The default
is the current directory when it is outside a Git repository; if the current
directory is inside a Git root, the wizard requires a separate path and does
not generate a sibling path or migrate the product repository. A valid
installation already present at the chosen root is not overwritten: the
wizard asks whether to manage it or choose another root.

Repository configuration is explicit. The keyboard checklist suggests only
immediate-child Git roots, with their current branches; use Up/Down to focus,
Space to select, and Enter to confirm up to 20 repositories. Nothing is added
without an explicit selection. **Add repository by path** accepts an explicitly
provided existing local Git root without widening discovery. **Create
greenfield repository** initializes selected empty paths only after approval;
that path collection remains text-based in this prototype. **Defer repository
configuration** leaves mappings empty. The wizard can still install
project-local adapter assets; an empty mapping is not reported as a first-run
readiness result.

For an existing selected Git root, the directory name suggests a stable ID,
project branch, and worktree mapping; the selected path and detected base
branch are shown. Each value remains editable and goes through the same
deterministic path, branch, symlink, overlap, and preflight validation. No
repository is inferred from the numeric keyboard or prompt position. The
wizard does not clone URLs, create worktrees, or change a product repository.
It writes only the repository mapping portion of `project.yaml`, preserving
unrelated content.

The next keyboard checklist shows all six registered adapters. Use Space to
toggle and Enter to confirm one or more. The first adapter selected is visibly
marked primary and continues to determine singleton runtime metadata and the
existing team/model setup behavior; the manifest's adapter membership is
normalized independently. Installing several adapters does **not** enable
per-Attempt cross-harness dispatch. Escape cancels repository selection and
backs out from adapter selection; Ctrl+C exits without applying the plan.
The registered adapters are OpenCode, Codex, Claude Code, GitHub Copilot,
Antigravity, and Hermes Agent.

After project adapters are selected, the wizard can optionally install the
Codex-native `$triad` skill and/or Hermes `/triad` wrapper at user level. It
resolves and displays every absolute file target (Codex: the native skill plus
`CODEX_HOME/triad-plus/host-entry-preflight.mjs`; Hermes: the active profile's
`skills/triad/` wrapper plus `~/.hermes/triad-plus/host-entry-preflight.mjs`).
It also displays an exact workspace-specific binding path for each selected
entry. That binding pins the canonical Control Workspace, its local manifest,
and expected project/global runtime bytes, and is written only after the owner
approves the exact final preview. Byte-identical shared bridge files are
labeled for reuse; workspace bindings are separate, so another approved
workspace does not replace an existing binding. A different existing file is
a preflight conflict and is never overwritten. The legacy
Codex `$CODEX_HOME/prompts/triad.md` file is never migrated, overwritten, or
deleted; if present, the wizard reports the name collision and blocks the
optional native skill install until the owner backs it up under another name
or deselects the Codex global entry. Skipping this step writes no user-level
files. An optional team-identity/model configuration may also be requested.
The concise first-run summary describes the proposed installation; type
`details` to inspect the exact file plan. When a user-level entry is selected,
reviewing `details` is required before `install` is accepted. The wizard does
not probe host executables or report project readiness. Type `install` to
apply the exact plan; any other answer cancels. Global bridge files are
written only after that final consent; no credentials or account settings are
changed. Direct global `init`/`upgrade`
and the legacy Codex/Hermes `install.sh --global` paths refuse the bridge so
they cannot bypass this preview.

Preflight refuses a Control Workspace inside a product Git root, unsafe paths,
and asset conflicts. Before applying, setup rechecks relevant root, role
configuration, and mapping state; the adapter commands also retain their
ownership and collision checks. A change detected after preview is not
silently overwritten.
Successful steps are not automatically rolled back if a later adapter install
fails; the wizard reports the partial result and directs the owner to inspect
it before re-entry. Setup does not create the root `PRD.md`,
`.loop/quality-gates.yaml`, repository baseline commits, or mapped worktrees,
and its first-run summary does not report readiness from them or assess their
quality. Selected repository/worktree mappings still undergo setup preflight
validation. `doctor` is a separate diagnostic for adapter installation, managed
project assets, the host executable, and available host/verifier
configuration; it does not establish project readiness or run quality gates.
Declared gates run later through `triad-verify` for a recorded Attempt.

### Existing-workspace management

Launching the wizard in a registered workspace defaults to its management
menu. To manage a workspace elsewhere, choose **Manage existing** and provide
its path explicitly. The menu offers list, add, doctor/status, upgrade,
remove, and exit. These are distinct from first-run onboarding:
`init` refuses to overwrite an existing installation, while
`upgrade --apply` is the managed update/repair path for an already
registered workspace.

List and doctor are read-only. Upgrade and remove are limited to adapters
recorded in that Control Workspace; add offers the registered adapters not
already recorded. Each mutation first runs the existing CLI dry-run/preflight,
then proceeds only when the exact word `apply` is entered. Cancellation or a
preflight conflict makes no changes. The plan reports project-local create,
reuse/shared, replacement/backup, removal, and preserved shared paths. Global
assets are not written or changed by these multi-adapter operations. Installing
an adapter still does not select it for the next Attempt; Attempt-bound host
dispatch remains unsupported.

Colors are used only for an interactive terminal and are disabled by
`NO_COLOR` or when output is not a TTY.

From an initialized Control Workspace, launch the wizard there to return to its
management menu and add another adapter without memorizing command names. The
menu displays installed membership and explicitly reports that this does not
select the host for the next Attempt.

For repeatable setup:

```bash
npx triad-plus
npx triad-plus doctor --host codex --control /path/to/project-control
```

Run the wizard from the intended Control Workspace (or supply its path in the
wizard) to review and optionally install the global bridge. The direct
`init --host codex --global` and `init --host hermes --global` commands do not
perform that installation.

## Version visibility

`--version` reports the package that is actually executing:

```bash
npx triad-plus --version
```

The workspace command reports the materialized installation recorded by the
control workspace manifest:

```bash
npx triad-plus version --control /path/to/project-control
```

An older workspace without `.triad-plus/installation.json` is reported as a
legacy installation. Triad+ does not infer a historical version from scattered
agent files.

## Installation manifest and safe uninstall

After a successful `init`, Triad+ writes
`.triad-plus/installation.json`. It records the selected adapter, CLI version,
project/global scopes, normalized managed-file paths, SHA-256 hashes, and a
manifest fingerprint. `upgrade --apply` refreshes this record after managed
assets are materialized; a legacy workspace receives a new manifest without
inventing its previous version.

Uninstall is dry-run by default:

```bash
npx triad-plus uninstall --host opencode --control /path/to/project-control
npx triad-plus uninstall --host opencode --control /path/to/project-control --apply
npx triad-plus uninstall --host opencode --control /path/to/project-control --global --apply
```

Only files listed in the manifest, still unchanged from their recorded hash,
are removed. Missing files are reported as `ABSENT`; modified assets are
preserved. Host directories are never pruned because directory ownership is
not claimed. The team configuration, `.loop/`, project manifest, feature
cards, artifacts, evidence, and other user state are preserved. A managed
`AGENTS.md` role-run block is tracked separately and removed only when its
markers and hash are exact; surrounding user content remains. A manifest
remains as an `uninstalled` or `partial` tombstone so a second uninstall is
idempotent and the ownership history is auditable.

`--global --apply` is deliberately preserve-by-default: global assets may be
shared by several control workspaces, so the command reports them as shared
and does not delete them without a cross-workspace ownership model.

Read-only commands require an existing control workspace; a typo path is
never created by `version` or `uninstall`.

### Local multi-adapter inventory

Schema-v1 workspaces remain readable as one adapter. `adapter list` and
`adapter doctor` do not write or migrate that record. A successful explicit
`adapter add <id> --control <path> --apply` migrates it to schema v2 and records
per-adapter managed assets plus exact shared-path owners. New multi-adapter
assets are project-local; no `--global` option is supported for these commands.
Additional adapter metadata is stored at
`.triad-runtime/adapters/<id>/adapter.json`; the existing
`.triad-runtime/adapter.json` is not rewritten when another host is added.
The terminal management menu is the recommended path. For scripts and advanced
use, this is the equivalent pinned CLI procedure from the initialized Control
Workspace; the first add is a dry run, and `--apply` performs the reviewed
project-local change:

```bash
npx triad-plus@1.19.0 adapter list --control .
npx triad-plus@1.19.0 adapter add copilot --control .
npx triad-plus@1.19.0 adapter add copilot --control . --apply
npx triad-plus@1.19.0 adapter doctor copilot --control .
npx triad-plus@1.19.0 adapter upgrade copilot --control .
npx triad-plus@1.19.0 adapter upgrade copilot --control . --apply
npx triad-plus@1.19.0 adapter remove copilot --control .
npx triad-plus@1.19.0 adapter remove copilot --control . --apply
```

`list`, `doctor`, and `version` are read-only. Add is a dry run without
`--apply`; repeating a healthy add is a no-op. Upgrade backs up only unchanged
managed files that it refreshes. Remove checks ownership and byte hashes before
deleting exclusive adapter files, retains shared paths, and aborts without
side effects when an asset was edited. Removing the final adapter retains the
v2 tombstone and all project/user state. Global assets in a legacy installation
are not changed by these local operations. Host binary availability is reported
separately from adapter membership.

The schema-v2 inventory is an installation/lifecycle foundation only. It does
not provide per-Attempt host selection or active-run safety. Attempts are not
dispatched to whichever adapter was most recently installed; host dispatch is
reported as unsupported until an explicit Attempt-bound liveness contract is
approved and implemented. Their optional global entry wrappers validate the
current project-local workspace after the host invokes the model; this is not a
pre-LLM security boundary, and native host discovery/invocation still requires
host-specific smoke testing.

## Upgrade, repair, or restore an existing control workspace

`init` is the first-install command and refuses to overwrite an existing
workspace. `upgrade --apply` is the managed update, repair, and restore path
for a workspace that is already registered by an installation manifest,
including a workspace whose project scope is `uninstalled` or `partial` after a
safe uninstall. It re-materializes project assets, reuses the preserved
`team.json`, and refreshes the manifest without changing user state, `.loop/`,
PRD files, evidence, or product repositories. The default is a dry run:

```bash
npx triad-plus upgrade --host codex --control /path/to/project-control
npx triad-plus upgrade --host codex --control /path/to/project-control --apply
```

This managed upgrade refreshes project-local assets. Codex/Hermes global entry
files are deliberately excluded from direct upgrade; their installation is
available only through the exact-path, final-consent first-run wizard.

Before replacing a managed asset, the applied upgrade saves its prior copy under
`.triad-plus/backups/`. Triad+ also maintains a clearly marked role-run block in
the control workspace `AGENTS.md`; existing instructions are preserved. Review
`doctor` output when host-level instructions impose a fixed identity, because a
higher-priority host policy can prevent the configured Orchestrator identity.

Supported hosts: `codex`, `opencode`, `claude-code`, `antigravity`, `hermes`, and
the `copilot` adapter. Other adapters retain their documented `--global`
behavior. Codex/Hermes entry files are the exception: only the interactive
first-run wizard installs them after exact-path preview and final consent. If
the control path is recognizably a product Git repository, setup stops unless
`--allow-product-repo` is explicitly supplied after review.

The saved `.triad-plus/team.json` separates stable role IDs from display names,
personas, models, and supported effort/options. Existing schema-version-1 team
files remain valid. Core roles are always enabled; Evaluator+ is enabled only
when `roles.evaluator.enabled` is `true`.

Setup silently reads existing mapped manifests into the inactive
`.triad-plus/quality-gates.draft.json`; no discovered commands or executable
probes run, and active catalogs remain unchanged. Existing drafts are preserved.
`npx triad-plus quality-gates --control .` shows a read-only preview;
`--refresh --apply` replaces only the draft, and `--lint` checks an active
catalog's structure without executing it. See
[quality-gate discovery](quality-gate-discovery.md) for limits and provenance.

The shared `triad-model-configuration` skill is installed with the selected
adapter. Ask the host agent to inspect or change a role model; it keeps
`.triad-plus/team.json` as the source of requested intent. Generated host assets
inherit host model/effort defaults; unverified requests are never native
overrides, even when their spelling looks plausible. Setup checks model ID
syntax without claiming catalog availability. Existing installations remove
old managed overrides through the normal preview/apply upgrade path. See
[model configuration](configuration.md#configure-models-through-the-agent).


| Role | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| Orchestrator | Maintains goal/context and decides the next step. |
| Developer | Changes the artifact to meet the declared card. |
| Reviewer | Finds defects and returns approved, rework, or blocked. |
| Evaluator+ | Optionally and freshly judges an approved result after the run. |

Open the control workspace and invoke the host-native command with an absolute
PRD path. The Orchestrator presents feature cards before implementation, then
delegates normal development and review. When `roles.evaluator.enabled` is true,
the Orchestrator invokes Evaluator+ automatically after Triad is approved. Users never create
evaluation packets, report paths, or evidence directories manually.

During a run the Orchestrator creates any Assignment Packet internally and
passes its explicit product-worktree dispatch context to the delegated roles;
there is no user-facing packet path to configure.

## Guided first entry

`npx triad-plus preflight --host <adapter> --control .` guides workspace
readiness; `--non-interactive --json` fails closed without explicit consent.
Native entries use the same contract and disclose post-LLM/capability limits.
Model intent remains separate from unverified host identity and unapplied role
overrides. See [universal readiness](universal-readiness.md) for copy/paste
approval steps, per-repository catalogs, receipt guards and the existing global
entry migration limitation. No partial onboarding release is implied.

# OpenCode adapter

Install with `npx triad-plus init --host opencode --control <path>`. Open the
control workspace and run `/triad <absolute-prd-path>`. Project-local agent and
command assets inherit the OpenCode host model and variant defaults.

Verification uses explicit Orchestrator dispatch. A configured Evaluator+ is
automatically invoked only after a Reviewer-approved result; it cannot reopen
that run.

`.triad-plus/team.json` records requested role models and effort as intent.
Triad+ omits unverified `model`/`variant` overrides from managed agents, so an
invalid requested ID cannot prevent `/triad` from loading. Upgrade existing
assets through `upgrade --apply` after reviewing its preview. Use OpenCode's
model picker to select an available host model; a saved request does not prove
that model was selected. Syntax checks require `provider/model` (optionally
`#variant`) and reject values such as `gpt 6 luna medium` without guessing a
replacement.

# Guida operativa Triad+

Triad+ è un metodo operativo per un coding-agent host. Non avvia daemon,
scheduler, database di workflow o una macchina a stati autonoma.

## Il metodo

```text
ready → in_progress → verifying → in_review → approved
                                      ├── rework → in_progress
                                      └── blocked
```

L’Orchestrator decide il prossimo passo e le escalation. Il Developer esegue un
tentativo delimitato. Il Reviewer decide `approved`, `rework` oppure `blocked`.

Prima del lavoro l’Orchestrator congela il PRD, dichiara card misurabili,
repository/worktree/branch e quality gate deterministici. Mostra il piano al
proprietario, poi delega normalmente sviluppo e review.

Per ogni assignment attivo può creare un Assignment Packet immutabile. Il
packet contiene il contesto delimitato della card e gli estratti pertinenti; il
host avvia il Developer con `cwd`/`workdir` uguale al product worktree
dichiarato, mantenendo espliciti i path del control workspace. Il Reviewer
riceve lo stesso packet più candidato/evidence. La rilettura completa di
PRD/ADR è solo fallback e le skill obbligatorie continuano a essere lette e
verificate tramite i loro path reali.

Dopo il completamento del Developer avviene la verifica: tramite hook validato
quando disponibile, altrimenti con dispatch esplicito dell’Orchestrator. Il
verifier esegue solo comandi `control-plane` dichiarati. L’evidence atomica lega
assignment ID/hash, run, branch del worktree, fingerprint del candidato, hash di
PRD/card e definizione dei gate. “I test passano” detto dall’agente è una claim;
l’output del verifier è evidence derivata dall’ambiente. Evidence fallita o
invalida non può essere trattata come pass.

Per Codex la modalità `auto` usa intenzionalmente il dispatch esplicito. Il
percorso asincrono `SubagentStop` resta disponibile solo come opt-in
sperimentale: gli hook producono evidence, mentre l’Orchestrator mantiene
l’autorità sull’avanzamento del loop.

L’adapter GitHub Copilot usa custom agent di progetto e la skill `triad`, con
dispatch esplicito della verification e senza hook di lifecycle. Lo smoke della
desktop app ha validato contesti distinti per i ruoli e la continuazione
unattended, oltre ai controlli CLI di asset e doctor.

Il Reviewer riceve card, diff, report Developer, rilievi precedenti ed evidence.
`rework` torna al Developer con una correzione delimitata; `blocked` richiede
all’Orchestrator di escalare la decisione. Le push normali possono essere autonome
dopo i goal dichiarati. La consegna formale al proprietario è un gate distinto:
registra push finale, eventuale valutazione, handoff, stato finale della run e
prova pratica prima di dichiarare il progetto consegnato. Avvio e stop della demo
restano del proprietario.

Una card può aggiungere una lista `required_gates` di gate ID del repository.
La lista è additiva: i gate globalmente obbligatori continuano a essere eseguiti,
quelli opzionali selezionati diventano obbligatori per la card e gli opzionali non
selezionati possono essere saltati. Lista assente o vuota mantiene il
comportamento legacy. Triad collega e registra gli ID senza attribuire loro un
significato visuale o di altro dominio.

## Target di qualità immutabile

Un progetto può optare per `project.quality_contract`, che collega al run un
fingerprint canonico del Quality Baseline JSON e verifica le source hashate prima
del dispatch e dei gate costosi. Drift o manifest invalido fermano il run come
contesto invalido senza consumare il budget di retry del prodotto. I criteri
`product_quality` vengono inviati al nuovo Evaluator+; quelli
`delivery_closure` sono verificati separatamente prima di `delivered`. Senza
questo opt-in i progetti legacy restano invariati.

## Retry e scope del candidato

Gli attempt sono record storici di esecuzione. I nuovi workspace separano e
limitano le transizioni di recovery runtime e di remediation del candidato: un
rework o uno scope cleanup non consuma il budget di recovery. Una card può
attivare un contratto deterministico sui path; il verifier confronta il delta
completo con il baseline originario della card prima dei gate costosi. Uno scope
PASS non sostituisce mai la review indipendente.

## Evaluator+

Evaluator+ è opzionale e fuori dal loop produttivo. Se abilitato in `team.json`,
l’Orchestrator lo avvia automaticamente dopo `approved`; osserva solo
goal, target di accettazione, candidato finale ed evidence del verifier. Produce
`PASS`, `FAIL` oppure `INDETERMINATE`. Un `FAIL` non modifica la run chiusa e non
avvia rework. Vedi [Evaluator+](evaluator-plus.md).

## Decisioni umane e record

Triad+ interpella il proprietario solo per criteri di successo mancanti, cambi di
scope/policy materiali, ambiguità non risolvibili, fallimenti ripetuti o demo
richieste. Conserva PRD immutabile, card, assignment, evidence, report di review,
eventuali report Evaluator+ e handoff in un workspace di controllo separato. Non
inserire token o segreti. Gli hook sono un’ottimizzazione, non autorità: il
dispatch esplicito della verification resta sempre disponibile. Vedi la
[matrice di compatibilità](compatibility.md).

Per ogni Card terminale l’Orchestrator può generare una vista deterministica
`card-reports/<card-id>.md` dai record canonici di Card, attempt, verifier e
Reviewer. Il renderer attribuisce al baseline completo della Card il delta dei
path modificati, inclusi rework, rinomina e cancellazione. L’handoff finale si
apre con un riepilogo leggibile e collega questi report, mantenendo anche le
evidence tecniche di delivery. I report sono scritti atomicamente, sono
ripetibili e usano riferimenti relativi: non sono una nuova source of truth né
una chiamata aggiuntiva a un agente. Il renderer va invocato esplicitamente con
il contesto derivato: la sua disponibilità non significa che
`card-reports/<card-id>.md` o `handoff.md` siano già stati materializzati.
Vedi la [guida ai report leggibili](human-readable-reports.md).

## Cockpit (sola lettura)

Quando il Control Workspace contiene già record di progetto, Card e attempt,
avvia `npx triad-plus cockpit` dalla sua directory principale. La directory
corrente viene validata; `--control <path>` seleziona un workspace diverso e
`--no-open` disabilita l'apertura automatica sicura del browser. Cockpit mostra
record persistiti ed evidence collegate; non avvia agenti e non genera i report
human-readable. Lo stato dichiarato `in_progress` non dimostra che un agente
sia attivo: Triad+ non registra la liveness degli agenti. Vedi la [guida del
Cockpit](../cockpit/README.md).

Per ogni demo configurata, registra nel progetto e nell’handoff comando, URL
locale, modalità di accesso remoto e URL remoto. `localhost` è solo locale: non
va indicato a chi prova da remoto. Avvia il servizio soltanto su richiesta del
proprietario e verifica l’URL remoto dichiarato prima di comunicarlo.

# Triad+ operating guide

Triad+ is an operating method for a coding-agent host. It does not run a daemon,
scheduler, workflow database, or autonomous state controller.

## The method

```text
ready → in_progress → verifying → in_review → approved
                                      ├── rework → in_progress
                                      └── blocked
```

The Orchestrator owns the next step and escalation. The Developer owns a bounded
implementation attempt. The Reviewer owns its `approved`, `rework`, or `blocked`
verdict.

Before work, the Orchestrator snapshots the PRD, declares measurable feature
cards, target repositories/worktrees/branches, and deterministic quality gates.
It shows the plan to the owner, then delegates ordinary development and review.

For each active assignment it may create an immutable Assignment Packet. The
packet carries the bounded card context and relevant excerpts; the host launches
the Developer with `cwd`/`workdir` equal to the declared product worktree, while
control-workspace paths remain explicit. The Reviewer receives the same packet
plus candidate/evidence. Full PRD/ADR reads are fallback-only, and mandatory
repository skills are still read and hash-verified from their real paths.

After Developer completion, verification happens through a validated host hook
when available, or explicit Orchestrator dispatch. The verifier executes only
declared `control-plane` commands. Atomic evidence binds assignment ID/hash, run,
worktree branch, candidate fingerprint, PRD/card hashes, and gate definition
hash. A developer saying tests pass is a claim; verifier output is
environment-derived evidence. Failed or invalid evidence cannot be treated as a
pass.

Codex is intentionally an exception to automatic hook selection: its `auto`
mode uses explicit dispatch. The async `SubagentStop` route remains an
experimental opt-in; this does not change the rule that hooks produce evidence
and the Orchestrator governs progress.

The GitHub Copilot adapter uses project custom agents and the `triad` skill,
with explicit verification dispatch and no lifecycle hook. Its desktop-app
smoke has validated distinct role contexts and unattended continuation in
addition to the CLI asset and doctor checks.

The Reviewer sees the card, diff, Developer report, previous findings, and
verifier evidence. `rework` returns a bounded finding to Developer; `blocked`
asks the Orchestrator to escalate the stated decision. Normal pushes may happen
autonomously once declared goals pass. A final owner delivery is a separate
closure gate: it records the final push, optional evaluation, handoff, final run
record, and practical test before the project is called delivered. Demo start and
stop remain owner-controlled.

Cards may add a `required_gates` list containing trusted repository gate IDs.
The list is additive: globally required gates still run, selected optional gates
become required for that card, and unselected optional gates may be skipped. An
absent or empty list preserves the legacy behavior. Triad binds and records the
IDs but does not attach visual or other domain-specific meaning to them.

## Immutable quality target

When a project opts in with `project.quality_contract`, the control plane binds a
canonical JSON Quality Baseline fingerprint and verifies its hashed sources before
dispatch or expensive gates. A source drift or invalid manifest stops the run as
context invalid, without consuming product retry budget. Product-quality criteria
are sent to the fresh Evaluator+ one at a time; delivery-closure criteria are
checked separately before `delivered`. The contract is optional, and legacy
projects without it are unchanged.

## Retry accounting and candidate scope

Attempts are historical execution records. New workspaces separately bound
runtime recovery and candidate remediation transitions; a rework or scope
cleanup does not consume recovery capacity. A card can opt in to a deterministic
path scope contract. The verifier checks the complete card delta against the
card's original baseline before expensive gates; a scope failure returns only a
bounded cleanup to Developer. A scope pass never replaces independent Reviewer
review.

## Evaluator+

Evaluator+ is optional and outside the production loop. When enabled in
`team.json`, the Orchestrator dispatches it automatically after `approved`. It
inspects only the goal, acceptance target, final candidate, and verifier evidence.
Its report is `PASS`, `FAIL`, or `INDETERMINATE`. A failure does not modify the
closed run or start repair. See [Evaluator+](evaluator-plus.md).

## Human decisions and records

Triad+ asks the owner only for missing success criteria, material scope/policy
changes, unresolved ambiguity, repeated failure, or a requested demo. Keep the
immutable PRD, cards, assignments, evidence, review reports, optional Evaluator+
reports, and handoff in a separate project-control workspace. Never place tokens
or secrets there. Hooks are an optimization, not authority; explicit verification
is always the fallback. See the [compatibility matrix](compatibility.md).

For every terminal Card, the Orchestrator may render a deterministic
`card-reports/<card-id>.md` view from the canonical Card, attempt, verifier, and
Reviewer records. The renderer attributes the complete changed-path delta to the
Card baseline, including rework, renames, and deletions. The final handoff opens
with a human-readable summary and links to those reports while retaining the
technical delivery evidence. Reports are atomic, repeatable, relative-path
views; they are not a new source of truth or an additional agent call. The
renderer must be explicitly invoked with derived context: an available
renderer does not mean `card-reports/<card-id>.md` or `handoff.md` has been
materialized. See the [human-readable reports guide](human-readable-reports.md).

## Cockpit (read-only)

Once a Control Workspace contains project, Card, and attempt records, run
`npx triad-plus cockpit` from its root. The current directory is validated;
`--control <path>` selects another workspace and `--no-open` disables safe
automatic browser opening. Cockpit shows persisted records and linked evidence;
it neither starts agents nor generates the human-readable reports. The state
`in_progress` is a declared workflow value, not proof that an agent is active.
Triad+ does not record agent liveness. See the [Cockpit guide](../cockpit/README.md).

For a configured demo service, record its command, local URL, remote-access mode,
and remote URL in the project and handoff. `localhost` is local-only; do not give
it to a remote tester as a reachable endpoint. Start the service only on the
owner's request and validate any declared remote URL before presenting it.

# PR planning and draft delivery

`triad-pr-plan` records a pre-run structural delivery intent and later turns an
Orchestrator snapshot into deterministic PR review groups. It supports `auto`,
`single`, `compact`, and `review-friendly` grouping (Auto is the default).
Structural approval binds project identity, byte-bound Card baselines,
canonical Card membership and grouping inputs, repository scope, dependencies,
and every group's exact branch/worktree/base/remote mapping. Its effect is
limited to draft-PR creation.

## Approve structure before implementation

This does not substitute for the normal Developer → Verifier → independent
Reviewer path or approve any Card. Before the first Developer assignment, the
Orchestrator can produce a structural snapshot and ask the owner to approve its
displayed plan once:

```sh
triad-pr-plan intent --project ./control --snapshot .loop/runtime/pr-structure.json \
  --mode auto --owner "Ainz Ooal Gown"
```

The snapshot must include byte-bound source entries for every Card and
`source_path`/`source_sha256` on each Card. The CLI prints the exact grouping
and bindings and records approval only after the owner types the displayed
structural digest phrase. Changing Card selection/membership, grouping inputs,
dependencies, repository declarations, project baseline, or any exact group
branch/worktree/base/remote binding requires a new approval. Queue execution
state, verifier/Reviewer evidence, test summaries, and final Card commits are
deliberately excluded, so ordinary run progress does not invalidate the
approved structure. Queue IDs/repository/dependencies, project repository
mappings, Card identities, and listed source bytes are rechecked against the
local Control Workspace.

## Refresh evidence and prepare drafts

After all Cards are approved and committed, refresh the snapshot from current
canonical evidence and reuse the saved intent:

```sh
triad-pr-plan preview --project ./control --snapshot .loop/runtime/pr-delivery-snapshot.json \
  --intent .loop/runtime/pr-structure-approval.json
triad-pr-plan draft --project ./control --snapshot .loop/runtime/pr-delivery-snapshot.json \
  --plan .loop/runtime/pr_plan.json --execute
```

The refreshed snapshot still binds every verifier and independent Reviewer
record by path and SHA-256. Existing execution preflight rechecks the actual
worktree, exact base-to-head commits, final Card commits, branch, remote and
remote base before creating any draft. A rework, missing/stale verifier,
unreviewed extra commit, wrong branch/base, structural drift, stacked
dependency, missing approval, or resume conflict fails closed. No Card
lifecycle transition or Reviewer semantics change.

For the approved-intent path, set `source.canonical_evidence: true` only in a
refreshed snapshot that includes the actual Assignment, verifier JSON,
completed Orchestrator Reviewer run record, bounded Reviewer result JSON, and
documentation-impact source in `source.files`. Draft preflight reads and
re-hashes those files, checks Assignment/run/Card identity bindings, requires
the actual Reviewer decision to be approved, and compares the verifier's
candidate file manifest to the actual final commit tree. A snapshot summary
alone is not sufficient evidence.

The current vertical slice deliberately does not create or populate grouped
delivery worktrees, cherry-pick commits, or push branches. If the approved
group branches/worktrees do not already contain exactly the approved Card
commits, the CLI stops at a concrete preflight blocker; it does not improvise a
branch lifecycle. The Orchestrator turns that blocker into the exact manual
handoff. This preserves the existing manual post-run workflow.

## Capability matrix and compact walkthrough

| Capability | Status in this slice | Boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Pre-run structural owner approval | Working, opt-in | Exact Cards, grouping, dependencies, repositories, and delivery bindings are approved once; existing projects are not implicitly opted in. |
| Post-run evidence refresh and validation | Working | Byte-bound queue/project/Card/Assignment/verifier/Reviewer/docs evidence and final commits are rechecked; candidate content must match the final commit tree. |
| Draft PRs for approved groups | Working when exact branches/worktrees are prepared | Exact base-to-head Card commit sets, branch, base, and remote are preflighted; creation is draft-only and retry-idempotent. |
| Group worktree creation, cherry-pick, and branch push | Manual / not implemented | The current project setup declares one project branch/worktree per repository; this slice does not add a grouped branch lifecycle. Missing exact group worktrees therefore need a concrete manual handoff. |
| Stacked PR dependencies | Unsupported | Cross-PR dependencies fail closed; stacked execution is not added. |
| Merge, release, or package publication | Not authorized / not implemented | The command creates draft PRs only. |

Walkthrough: (1) snapshot canonical Cards and repository bindings, then run
`intent` and record the owner's structural digest approval before any Developer
assignment; (2) run the unchanged Card lifecycle; (3) refresh a terminal
snapshot from canonical evidence and run `preview --intent`; (4) run
`draft --execute` only after evidence and Git preflight pass. A group that lacks
its exact prepared branch/worktree stops before any PR write. The CLI shows
expected path count versus the configured review limit as a review-burden
proxy; no wall-clock overhead benchmark was collected in this slice.

The JSON snapshot contains `project_id`, `canonical_card_ids`, `repositories`,
`cards`, and `source`. `source` names the current `work-queue.yaml` and
`project.yaml` paths and SHA-256 values, plus a `files` manifest containing
every byte-bound source/evidence file. Each repository entry includes its
declared `id`, `path`, `worktree`, `base_branch`, `project_branch`,
`base_commit`, `remote`, and exact `remote_url`. Each Card includes its
selected state, dependencies, expected/changed paths, and source binding;
completed Cards additionally carry final commit metadata, passing verifier
evidence, independent Reviewer approval, test summary, and documentation-impact
review. For each draft group, the group's `base_commit` remains the PR base and
preflight requires the complete `base_commit..HEAD` commit set to equal exactly
one distinct `final.commit` from every approved Card in that group. A Card's
candidate is independently checked from its own `final.base_commit`; that
baseline must be the group base or an earlier approved Card commit in the same
ancestry, and must be an ancestor of the Card's final commit. Extra commits
fail closed even when they only touch paths already present in the approved
Card delta.

When a mode produces more than one group for a repository, `group_bindings`
maps each deterministic group id to its own `branch`, `worktree`, `base_branch`,
`base_commit`, `remote`, and `remote_url`. Generate group ids with
`prGroupId(repositoryId, cardIds)` from `runtime/lib/pr-planning.mjs`.
`single` means one group per target repository, not one PR across unrelated
repositories.

The legacy post-run approval workflow remains available:

```sh
triad-pr-plan preview --project ./control --snapshot .loop/runtime/pr-snapshot.json --mode auto
triad-pr-plan approve --project ./control --snapshot .loop/runtime/pr-snapshot.json --plan .loop/runtime/pr_plan.json --owner "Ainz Ooal Gown"
triad-pr-plan draft --project ./control --snapshot .loop/runtime/pr-snapshot.json --plan .loop/runtime/pr_plan.json
triad-pr-plan draft --project ./control --snapshot .loop/runtime/pr-snapshot.json --plan .loop/runtime/pr_plan.json --execute
```

With `preview --intent`, the approved grouping and bindings are reused without
a second owner prompt, while the refreshed evidence snapshot is still fully
validated. Without `--intent`, the legacy flow behaves unchanged. Legacy
`approve` prints the exact repository/group scope and requires the owner to
type `approve <first-12-plan-hash-characters>`; that approval is invalidated if
the snapshot or plan drifts. `draft` without `--execute` performs read-only Git
preflight (including remote-ref checks) and makes no GitHub CLI calls.
`draft --execute` requires a valid structural intent or legacy plan approval,
an already-pushed clean group branch, an unchanged remote base, a matching
repository remote, complete byte-bound evidence, and available GitHub CLI
authentication. It creates GitHub draft PRs only and records each result
locally. A plan/group marker makes retries idempotent; unmatched existing PRs
or cross-PR dependencies fail closed for manual recovery. It never pushes
branches, merges, publishes releases, or installs or changes authentication.

All input and output plan paths must remain inside the selected Control
Workspace. Non-GitHub remotes are returned as manual handoffs rather than
automatically published.

# Immutable Quality Contract

Triad+ 1.8 optionally binds a run to an owner-approved, machine-readable
Quality Baseline. It is an additional target record, not a second control
plane and not a replacement for the PRD, card baseline, or candidate
fingerprint.

```text
Quality Baseline fingerprint  = what the run was meant to satisfy
Repository/card baseline     = where implementation started
Candidate fingerprint        = what implementation produced
```

## Manifest

The manifest is JSON and is normally stored at
`artifacts/quality-baseline.json`:

```json
{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "id": "my-project-quality-baseline",
  "revision": 1,
  "sources": [
    {
      "id": "prd",
      "role": "intent",
      "path": "artifacts/prd.md",
      "sha256": "<64-hex-digest>"
    }
  ],
  "criteria": [
    { "id": "QB-001", "scope": "product_quality", "requirement": "..." },
    { "id": "QB-010", "scope": "delivery_closure", "requirement": "..." }
  ],
  "fingerprint": "<sha256-of-canonical-manifest-without-fingerprint>"
}
```

The manifest requires a positive revision, at least one source, unique source
and criterion IDs, project-relative source paths, SHA-256 for every source, and
non-empty requirements. Version 1 has exactly two criterion scopes:
`product_quality` and `delivery_closure`.

The fingerprint is SHA-256 over canonical JSON with object keys sorted
recursively, array order preserved, and the `fingerprint` field excluded from
the payload. Whitespace and object formatting therefore do not change it.

## Binding and drift

When `project.quality_contract` is present, the Orchestrator binds both the
manifest path and its fingerprint in every active Developer assignment:

```json
{
  "quality_baseline_path": "artifacts/quality-baseline.json",
  "expected_quality_baseline_fingerprint": "<sha256>"
}
```

`triad-verify` validates the manifest and all source hashes before expensive
gates. A malformed manifest or fingerprint mismatch is
`quality_baseline_invalid`; a valid manifest whose declared sources or
assignment fingerprint no longer match is `quality_baseline_drift`. Both are
`invalid_context`: no Developer dispatch, expensive gates, or retry budget.

Projects without `quality_contract` retain the legacy PRD-only path. A
rebaseline is never an in-place edit: create a new revision/fingerprint and
record an explicit lineage event. Historical evidence is not silently
reinterpreted.

## Phase ownership

`product_quality` criteria are included in the fresh, blind Evaluator+ packet.
The packet carries the baseline fingerprint, final candidate fingerprint,
criteria, approved source material, and bounded verifier evidence. It never
includes delivery criteria, queue state, handoff state, or attempt history.

Evaluator+ returns one result per product criterion. The control plane validates
coverage, uniqueness, scope, candidate/baseline fingerprints, and the overall
verdict. Aggregation is deterministic:

```text
any FAIL               -> FAIL
else any INDETERMINATE -> INDETERMINATE
else                   -> PASS
```

`delivery_closure` criteria are evaluated separately during delivery closure
and recorded with criterion ID, verdict, and evidence references. A run is not
`delivered` when any configured delivery criterion is `FAIL` or
`INDETERMINATE`. Quality Bar evaluation is not a required-gate replacement,
and an Evaluator+ failure never repairs or reopens Triad automatically.

## Explicit control-plane validation

The installed runtime exposes deterministic commands for the two phase
boundaries. Run the baseline preflight before dispatch, then run the phase
validators from the control workspace so the baseline is reloaded from disk:

```bash
node .triad-runtime/triad-evaluator-validate.mjs --mode baseline \
  --project /absolute/path/to/control \
  --baseline artifacts/quality-baseline.json

node .triad-runtime/triad-evaluator-validate.mjs --mode evaluator \
  --project /absolute/path/to/control \
  --baseline artifacts/quality-baseline.json \
  --result artifacts/evaluator-plus/evaluation.json \
  --expected-candidate-fingerprint <final-candidate-fingerprint>

node .triad-runtime/triad-evaluator-validate.mjs --mode delivery \
  --project /absolute/path/to/control \
  --baseline artifacts/quality-baseline.json \
  --result artifacts/delivery-closure.json
```

Each command emits one machine-readable JSON result and exits non-zero for an
invalid contract, source drift, stale candidate binding, or invalid result.

# Inactive quality-gate discovery

Setup reads the explicitly mapped repositories and prepares
`.triad-plus/quality-gates.draft.json`. This is an **inactive proposal**, not
readiness, execution evidence or an approved catalog. It never replaces
`.loop/quality-gates.yaml`, installs dependencies, probes executables or runs
discovered commands. The behavior is shared by all six adapters.

```bash
# Fresh read-only preview; no files changed and no commands executed.
npx triad-plus quality-gates --control .

# Explicitly refresh only the inactive draft; active catalogs stay unchanged.
npx triad-plus quality-gates --control . --refresh --apply

# Lint an owner-configured catalog without executing it or probing versions.
npx triad-plus quality-gates --control . --lint
npx triad-plus quality-gates --control . --lint --source .loop/gates/backend.json
```

The commands do not prompt. Invalid arguments, unsafe/unreadable catalog paths
and lint failures exit nonzero. An empty proposal is a discovery result, not
READY. Existing drafts are preserved byte-for-byte during installation;
replacement requires `--refresh --apply`. Unchanged refreshes are idempotent.
The wizard's detailed preview names the draft file before installation.

## Sources, categories and limits

The supported automatic source is `package.json` npm scripts. Explicit script
names classify candidates as test, lint, typecheck or build; Triad+ does not
invent a command from a language or directory name. Script bodies must use a
supported single runner invocation. Shell composites/substitutions, inline
Node code, missing or unsafe Node script files, pre/post lifecycle hooks,
watch/server modes, publish/deploy/install, Docker, VRT, snapshot update and
mutating fix/write/clean commands are excluded conservatively. Other package
managers and unsupported forms need manual configuration. Common non-Node
manifests are noted for manual review; their contents are not interpreted.

Each candidate records its exact script name, manifest and script SHA-256,
category and prerequisites. Its proposed command is
`npm --ignore-scripts run <script-name>` with a 600-second timeout. npm still
runs that explicitly named script, while omitting its pre/post hooks
([npm configuration reference](https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v11/using-npm/config/#ignore-scripts)).
Discovery additionally excludes scripts that declare such hooks; the flag is
defense in depth, not a certification that the script is safe.

Manifest bodies, arbitrary script text, OS error bodies, credentials and
environment values are not copied into the draft or console output. Paths and
script names remain data, never agent instructions. Regular-file reads are
bounded to 1 MiB, mappings to 64 repositories and script maps to 128 entries;
symlink and special-file sources are rejected. Dependency availability and
executable identity are not attested by discovery.

## Repository and worktree binding

Each mapping has its own proposal. If its declared worktree exists, discovery
reads that worktree's manifest. If it does not exist, the repository manifest
is labeled **repository-preview**, with an instruction to re-discover in the
worktree before confirmation. An unsafe existing worktree never falls back to
the repository. Reading either directory does not verify its Git identity or
branch: `context_verified` stays false until a separate readiness check.

Do not merge commands from different repositories into one catalog running in
one worktree. The verifier already executes an assignment's catalog in that
assignment's worktree and binds its hash through `assignment.gates_path`.
`command_source` is discovery metadata, not the verifier's native executable
`toolchain`/`provenance` binding. A proposal is rejected by the verifier even
with a matching hash; do not use it as `gates_path` or copy it over an active
catalog.

## Review, execution and subsequent onboarding

An owner must review the manifest and prerequisites and select, edit or reject
candidates before constructing an active per-repository catalog. Discovery/inspection never activates a command. The separate
[guided preflight](universal-readiness.md) re-discovers current sources and
requires explicit owner consent before creating/binding a per-repository
catalog. A saved draft is not evidence of approval. Manual active-catalog
configuration remains available, but newly onboarded assignments must bind the
exact owner-approved path/hash and current worktree/branch/source state.

Lint accepts the existing JSON / list-of-maps YAML contract, rejects missing,
duplicate or placeholder commands, malformed fields, unsupported YAML blocks
and invalid toolchain bindings, and bounds timeout values to 1..3600 seconds
(600 by default). It validates structure only: it does not prove command
safety, tool availability, worktree readiness or a gate pass. The deterministic
verifier still resolves provenance and executes approved gates independently
of Reviewer conclusions.

Regression evidence is in [gate-discovery-test.mjs](../tests/gate-discovery-test.mjs)
and the real PTY setup integration. Fixtures cover six adapters, separate
repository/worktree manifests, missing/malformed/malicious sources, no execution
or secret disclosure, active-file preservation, explicit refresh and inactive
proposal rejection. No native host session or complete `/triad` E2E is claimed
by these tests.
